info.title: stingray
info.description: OpenTail.Stingray command-line interface — LLM inference and image generation using GGUF models, with CPU/Vulkan/CUDA backends. Install with `dotnet tool install -g OpenTail.Stingray.Cli`.

commands.name: admit-arch
commands.description:
Triage a GGUF whose architecture is not yet allowlisted: tokenizer/tensor
inventory, a real bypassed forward-pass run, and (with --reference-tokens)
a formatted ADMIT/REJECT verdict.

options.name: --help
options.description: Prints help information

options.name: --model
options.description: GGUF to evaluate

options.name: --prompt
options.description: Raw prompt to tokenize and greedy-decode (no chat template applied)

options.name: --tokens
options.description: Number of greedy tokens to generate

options.name: --reference-tokens
options.description:
Comma-separated reference token ids (from llama.cpp or another oracle)
to compare against, e.g. from `llama-server .../completion` with
return_tokens:true

options.name: --golden
options.description:
Golden reference file (written by capture-golden): recorded prompt
token ids and llama.cpp continuation. Runs BEFORE the allowlist gate,
so an already-admitted architecture can be re-verified, and no
tokenizer is involved.

commands.name: calibrate
commands.description:
Time the expert kernels (CPU, copy, GPU) on this machine and print where
expert work should run

options.name: --help
options.description: Prints help information

options.name: --seconds
options.description: Window per measurement in seconds (default 2)

options.name: --no-gpu
options.description: Skip the GPU measurements

options.name: --tokens
options.description: Rows per expert for the prefill measurement (default 93, the OLMoE average)

options.name: --no-save
options.description: Print only; do not write the profile

commands.name: capabilities
commands.description: Show which model-package profiles, dtypes and backends are supported

options.name: --help
options.description: Prints help information

commands.name: capture-golden
commands.description:
Capture a golden reference from the vendored llama.cpp: oracle-tokenized
prompt ids, greedy continuation from llama-server, model SHA-256; writes a
small JSON with no machine paths. Check it later with admit-arch --golden.

options.name: --help
options.description: Prints help information

options.name: --model
options.description: GGUF to capture a reference for

options.name: --prompt
options.description:
Raw prompt text, tokenized by llama-tokenize (the model's own BOS
behaviour applies)

options.name: --prompt-ids
options.description: Comma-separated prompt token ids, used as-is instead of tokenizing

options.name: --tokens
options.description: Tokens to generate

options.name: --mode
options.description:
How the golden is checked later: free (greedy run compared until it
diverges) or teacherForced (reference tokens fed, every position
compared)

options.name: --case
options.description:
Name of this case inside the golden (an existing case of the same
name is replaced)

options.name: --out
options.description:
Golden file to write (default: ./<architecture>.golden.json); an
existing file for the same model gets the case added

options.name: --source
options.description:
Where the checkpoint came from (Hugging Face repo id), recorded in
the golden

options.name: --notes
options.description:
Provenance notes recorded in the golden (no paths: the file is
checked for machine-specific text)

options.name: --server
options.description:
llama-server executable (default: tools/llama.cpp/llama-server.exe
found upward from here)

options.name: --tokenizer
options.description:
llama-tokenize executable (default:
tools/llama.cpp/llama-tokenize.exe found upward from here)

options.name: --server-timeout
options.description: How long to wait for llama-server to load the model

options.name: --expect
options.description:
Hyperparameter guards to pin in the golden, e.g.
ropeDim=16,numExperts=8,hasFfnBias=true (ModelHyperparams
property=value, comma separated)

options.name: --min-confident
options.description:
Require at least N matches at positions where the reference itself
was confident (evidence requirement for teacher-forced cases)

options.name: --no-hash
options.description:
Skip the SHA-256 of the model (the golden then cannot pin the file;
slow for large checkpoints)

commands.name: gguf-transplant
commands.description:
Build a mixed-precision GGUF by copying a base checkpoint and taking
selected tensors (regex) from a donor checkpoint; verifies the result
byte-for-byte

options.name: --help
options.description: Prints help information

options.name: --base
options.description: GGUF whose header, metadata and (non-replaced) tensors are kept

options.name: --donor
options.description:
GGUF supplying the replacement tensors (same tensor names and dimensions as the
base)

options.name: --tensors
options.description: Regex matched against base tensor names; matching tensors are taken from the donor

options.name: --out
options.description: Output GGUF path (must not be the base or donor; must not exist unless --force)

options.name: --force
options.description: Overwrite the output if it exists

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: Print the replacement plan and the resulting size, write nothing

commands.name: image
commands.description:
Generate an image from a text prompt using a native FLUX or Z-Image-Turbo
diffusion pipeline (VAE + CLIP-L + T5-XXL + DiT GGUF). See
'opentail-llm-cli image --help' for required model paths.

options.name: --help
options.description: Prints help information

options.name: --model
options.description:
Path to diffusion model GGUF or safetensors directory
(FLUX.1, Z-Image-Turbo, …)

options.name: --prompt
options.description: Text prompt describing the image to generate

options.name: --negative-prompt
options.description: Negative prompt — what to avoid in the generated image

options.name: --vae
options.description:
Path to VAE safetensors file or directory
(ae.safetensors or vae/ dir)

options.name: --qwen-encoder
options.description:
(Z-Image) Path to Qwen3-4B GGUF text encoder (from
Qwen/Qwen3-4B-GGUF)

options.name: --qwen-tokenizer
options.description: (Z-Image) Path to Qwen3 tokenizer.json

options.name: --umt5-encoder
options.description:
(Wan) Path to the real UMT5-XXL text encoder
safetensors (converted from Wan-AI/Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B's
models_t5_umt5-xxl-enc-bf16.pth)

options.name: --umt5-tokenizer
options.description:
(Wan) Path to the real UMT5 tokenizer.json
(Wan-AI/Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B's
google/umt5-xxl/tokenizer.json)

options.name: --n-gpu-layers
options.description:
(Z-Image) GPU acceleration: -1 = auto (CUDA→Vulkan→CPU,
default), 0 = CPU only

options.name: --device
options.description:
(Z-Image) GPU to use: auto (default), none/cpu, an
index (0, 1), or a named device (CUDA0, Vulkan1)

options.name: --backend
options.description:
(Z-Image) Force compute backend: auto (default), cuda,
vulkan, cpu

options.name: --clip-l
options.description: (FLUX) Path to CLIP-L encoder safetensors

options.name: --clip-g
options.description:
(SD3/3.5) Path to OpenCLIP-bigG encoder safetensors --
when given together with --clip-l and --vae, -m is read
as the standalone MMDiT transformer safetensors (the
standard diffusers multi-file layout) instead of a
single combined checkpoint

options.name: --clip-tokenizer
options.description: (FLUX) Path to CLIP tokenizer.json

options.name: --t5xxl
options.description: (FLUX) Path to T5-XXL encoder safetensors

options.name: --t5-tokenizer
options.description: (FLUX) Path to T5 tokenizer.json

options.name: --width
options.description:
Output image width in pixels — must be divisible by 16
(default: 512)

options.name: --height
options.description: Output image height in pixels — must be divisible by 16

options.name: --steps
options.description:
Denoising steps (default: 4 for Z-Image-Turbo, 4 for
FLUX schnell, 20 for dev)

options.name: --cfg-scale
options.description:
Guidance scale — not used for Z-Image (distilled), 1.0
for FLUX schnell (default: auto)

options.name: --seed
options.description: RNG seed (-1 = random, default: -1)

options.name: --output
options.description: Output PNG file path (default: output.png)

options.name: --upscaler
options.description:
Path to ESRGAN/Real-ESRGAN upscaler weights
(.safetensors). Upscales the generated image by ×2 or
×4 before saving.

options.name: --upscale-blend
options.description:
Blend factor for the upscaled result (0.0–1.0). 1.0 =
full RRDB (sharpest), <1.0 softens by blending with
bicubic. Default 1.0.

options.name: --verbose
options.description: Show per-step timing and progress (default: False)

options.name: --init-image
options.description:
Path to initial image for image-to-image (img2img)
generation

options.name: --mask-image
options.description:
Path to inpainting mask image (white = inpaint region,
black = preserve original)

options.name: --strength
options.description:
Strength for img2img generation (0.0 to 1.0, default:
0.75). Higher values add more variation from the
initial image.

options.name: --sampler
options.description:
Diffusion scheduler algorithm: euler (default),
euler-a, ddim, dpm2m, dpm2m-karras, lcm

options.name: --control-net
options.description: Path to ControlNet weights (.safetensors or .gguf)

options.name: --control-image
options.description:
Path to ControlNet condition hint image (Canny edge,
depth map, openpose, etc.)

options.name: --control-strength
options.description: ControlNet conditioning scale/strength (default: 1.0)

options.name: --video-frames
options.description:
Number of video frames to generate for Wan video

options.name: --use-sdcpp
options.description:
Delegate to stable-diffusion.cpp sd-cli instead of

options.name: --sd-cli
options.description:
Path to sd-cli executable used when --use-sdcpp is set

options.name: --text-encoder
options.description:
Path to the LLM-style text encoder GGUF (FLUX.2:

commands.name: perplexity
commands.description:
Teacher-forced perplexity over a text file (llama.cpp llama-perplexity
analogue; CPU only). Reports mean NLL, perplexity, and position-bucket NLLs
â the TurboQuant/KVarN accuracy gate (issue #180).

options.name: --help
options.description: Prints help information

options.name: --model
options.description: Path to GGUF model file

options.name: --file
options.description:
UTF-8 text file to evaluate (llama.cpp -f/--file).
Tokenized raw (no chat template); the first -c tokens
are scored.

options.name: --ctx-size
options.description:
Number of tokens to evaluate (default: 2048). Clamped
to the model context length and the corpus length.

options.name: --tq
options.description:
Enable TurboQuant KV cache compression (same flag as
the run command) (default: False)

options.name: --tq-mode
options.description:
TurboQuant quantizer for --tq: auto (default: kvarn
where supported, else lloydmax with a quality warning),
kvarn (issue #180: 4-bit K / 2-bit V, 128-token tiles),
or lloydmax (3-bit codebooks; severely degrades quality
on QK-norm models such as Qwen3 — issue #432).

options.name: --tq-window
options.description:
FP32 recent-token window before compression kicks in
(default: 256; min 128 for kvarn — one full tile). Also
sets the first position-bucket edge of the report, so
pass the same value to the fp32 baseline for
bucket-comparable numbers.

options.name: --n-gpu-layers
options.description:
Layers on GPU: 0 (default, CPU forward pass) or -1
(full offload — CUDA via CudaForwardPass, else Vulkan
via GpuForwardPass). Partial offload is not supported.

options.name: --backend
options.description:
With -g -1, which GPU backend to score on: 'cuda' or
'vulkan'. Default: CUDA when present, else Vulkan.
Needed on machines with both to gate the Vulkan path
explicitly.

options.name: --batched
options.description:
Score every position through batched
ForwardPass.Prefill (docs/cpu-prefill-plan.md §14)
instead of token-by-token Forward. Default mode NEVER
calls MatMulBatched, so it cannot see
STINGRAY_CPU_PREFILL_Q8's effect at all -- this flag is
required to actually measure that path's perplexity
impact. Not supported with --tq or -g -1;
per-layer-head-dim (gemma-4) and MoE models ARE
supported (MoE routes through the batched per-expert
FFN). Prompts are evaluated in --batch-chunk-size
chunks so KV-cache truncation matches real multi-chunk
prefill.

options.name: --batch-chunk-size
options.description:
Tokens per Prefill() call in --batched mode (default:
256, matching the engine's STINGRAY_PREFILL_CHUNK
default). Smaller chunks exercise more chunk-boundary
KV-cache transitions; larger chunks are closer to a
single-shot prompt.

options.name: --dump-nll
options.description:
Write one line per scored position to this file: target
position, target token id, NLL. For diffing per-token
log-probs against a reference (e.g. llama-server) to
find which tokens carry a PPL gap.

commands.name: pull
commands.description:
Download a GGUF model from Hugging Face by repo id, e.g. `stingray pull -r
bartowski/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-GGUF`

options.name: --help
options.description: Prints help information

options.name: --repo
options.description:
Hugging Face repo id, e.g. bartowski/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-GGUF (a full
https://huggingface.co/... URL also works)

options.name: --quant
options.description:
Case-insensitive substring to pick among multiple .gguf files (e.g.
Q4_K_M). Default: prefer Q4_K_M, then Q4_K_S, Q5_K_M, Q8_0, else the
first listed.

options.name: --revision
options.description:
Commit, branch or tag to download from. Default: the repo's current
head, resolved to its commit SHA first and then used for every file, so
the files you get are the ones that were listed. Pass the commit `scout
-r` printed to fetch exactly what it inspected.

options.name: --out
options.description: Destination directory (default: ./models)

options.name: --list
options.description: List available .gguf files in the repo and exit, without downloading

options.name: --model

options.name: --file

command-line limit.

options.name: --image
options.description:
Path to a PNG image for multimodal input
(Gemma 4 encoder-free vision). Repeatable for
multiple images; reference each with an
<image> marker in -p (left-to-right), or omit
markers to prepend them. Requires --mmproj
and a text prompt (-p). Runs on CPU, CUDA
(full + partial offload), and Vulkan (full
offload).

options.name: --mmproj
options.description:
Path to the multimodal projector GGUF
(mmproj-*.gguf). Required with --image.
Mirrors llama.cpp's --mmproj.

options.name: --n-predict
options.description: Number of tokens to predict (default: 512)

options.name: --temp
options.description: Temperature (0 = greedy, default: 0.7)

options.name: --top-k
options.description: Top-k sampling (0 = disabled, default: 40)

options.name: --top-p
options.description: Top-p nucleus sampling (default: 0.95)

options.name: --min-p
options.description: Min-p sampling (default: 0.05)

options.name: --seed
options.description: RNG seed (-1 = random, default: -1)

options.name: --single-turn
options.description:
Generate one response and exit (default:
False)

options.name: --system-prompt
options.description: System prompt

options.name: --no-display-prompt
options.description: Don't echo the prompt (default: False)

options.name: --verbose-prompt
options.description: Print token IDs before generating (default:

options.name: --n-gpu-layers
options.description:
Layers on GPU (0=CPU only, -1=all). Mirrors
llama.cpp's --n-gpu-layers/--ngl.

options.name: --device
options.description:
GPU device to offload to: index (0,1,…), name
(CUDA0, Vulkan1), or 'none' for CPU. Default:
auto. Single-device only (no multi-GPU
split). Mirrors llama.cpp's --device.

options.name: --ctx-size
options.description:
Context size / max sequence length (0 = model
default)

options.name: --tq
options.description:
Enable TurboQuant KV cache compression
(reduces KV memory ~4-8x; quantizer picked by
--tq-mode) (default: False)

options.name: --tq-mode
options.description:
TurboQuant quantizer for --tq: auto (default:
kvarn where supported, else lloydmax with a
quality warning), kvarn (issue #180:
Sinkhorn-normalized asymmetric RTN, 4-bit K /
2-bit V, 128-token tiles; CPU (-g 0, any
power-of-2 head dim ≤ 1024) or
full-CUDA-offload dense (-g -1, head dim ≤
256); no SnapKV), or lloydmax (3-bit
Lloyd-Max codebooks; severely degrades
quality on QK-norm models such as Qwen3 —
issue #432).

options.name: --cache-type-k
options.description:
KV-cache element type for the CUDA backend:
fp32 (default), bf16 (half the KV VRAM → ~2x
context), or q8_0 (quarter → ~4x). OpenTail
applies one dtype to both K and V, so -ctk
and -ctv must agree. Mirrors llama.cpp
--cache-type-k/-ctk. Env: STINGRAY_KV_DTYPE.

options.name: --cache-type-v
options.description:
KV-cache V-cache element type. Must match
--kv-type/--cache-type-k/-ctk: OpenTail
applies one dtype to both K and V. Mirrors
llama.cpp --cache-type-v/-ctv.

options.name: --draft-model
options.description:
Path to a smaller draft model for speculative
decoding (greedy only, requires --temp 0).
Mirrors llama.cpp's --model-draft.

options.name: --spec-lookahead
options.description:
Number of draft tokens per speculative step
with --draft-model (default: 4)

options.name: --draft-lookup
options.description:
Speculative decoding via prompt-lookup
(n-gram) drafting — proposes tokens by
matching the generated tail against
prompt+history; no draft model needed (greedy
only, requires --temp 0) (default: False)

options.name: --spec-type
options.description:
Speculative decoding type: auto (default;
enables MTP when supported), none, mtp
(alias: draft-mtp), dspark (requires
--dspark-model). Mirrors llama.cpp.

options.name: --dspark-model
options.description:
Path to a DSpark draft-head model.safetensors
(deepseek-ai/DeepSpec, e.g.
dspark_qwen3_4b_block7) with its config.json
alongside. Enables DSpark block-speculative
decoding (greedy only, CPU target for now —
PR #413 spec).

options.name: --dspark-place
options.description:
Where the DSpark draft head runs: auto
(default; planner decides from VRAM/RAM
headroom), gpu, cpu, off. Unset resolves via
STINGRAY_DSPARK_PLACE. An explicit value pins
the mode outright, like -g pins the layer
split.

options.name: --dspark-verify-len
options.description:
Cap on draft tokens verified per DSpark step.
Unset resolves via
STINGRAY_DSPARK_VERIFY_LEN, then 0 = the
confidence scheduler decides (up to the
head's block size). (default: 0)

options.name: --dspark-min-confidence
options.description:
Floor on the DSpark confidence head's
predicted acceptance probability; positions
below it are trimmed from the verify batch.
STINGRAY_DSPARK_MIN_CONFIDENCE, then 0 =
verify the whole block. (default: -1)

options.name: --spec-draft-n-max
options.description:
Max draft tokens per MTP step (issue #30
batched verify). Unset resolves via
STINGRAY_MTP_DRAFT_N, then defaults to 1 (a
2-token verify batch — the measured optimum).
Values > 1 also need snapshot-ring slots: set
STINGRAY_MTP_BATCH_MAX >= drafts+1 (default
2; each extra slot costs ~150 MiB VRAM on
27B). Mirrors llama.cpp.

options.name: --spec-draft-n-min
options.description:
Min draft tokens per MTP step (default: 0).
Mirrors llama.cpp. Currently rejected at
parse time when > 0 since N=1 is the only
supported draft length; issue #37.

options.name: --spec-draft-p-min
options.description:
Min draft probability for MTP probabilistic
accept (default: 1.0 = strict argmax-match,
byte-identical to no-MTP baseline). 0.75
mirrors llama.cpp; values in (0, 1) accept
drafts whose softmax probability under the
verifier meets the threshold even when they
aren't argmax (issue #38).

options.name: --min-batch-blas
options.description:
Minimum batch size to use OpenBLAS SGEMM in
MatMulBatched (default: 16, crossover for
Q4_K_M weights). Also settable via
STINGRAY_MIN_BATCH_BLAS env var.

options.name: --prefill-dequant-cache-mb
options.description:
Legacy dequant-once BLAS weight-cache setting
(issue #189). Currently dormant because the
CPU prefill kernels do not use the OpenBLAS
route; this option does not change inference
math. CPU only. (default:

options.name: --repeat-penalty
options.description:
Repetition penalty (1.0 = disabled, >1.0

Mirrors llama.cpp's
--repeat-penalty/--repeat_penalty.

options.name: --repeat-last-n
options.description:
Number of recent tokens the repetition
penalty considers (default: 64; 0 = disabled;

options.name: --threads
options.description:
CPU worker threads for the SIMD kernels
(default: logical processor count, or
STINGRAY_CPU_THREADS). Mirrors llama.cpp's
-t/--threads.

options.name: --escape
options.description:
Process escape sequences (\n, \t, \r, \\) in

(default: False)

options.name: --logit-bias
options.description:
Additive logit bias for a token. Format:

'1234+1.5' or '5678-100'. Repeatable. Mirrors
llama.cpp's --logit-bias.

options.name: --chat-template
options.description:
Override the model's built-in chat template
with a raw Jinja2 source string. Named
shortcuts (chatml, llama3, …) are refused —
hand-written approximations degrade output
silently. Mirrors llama.cpp's

options.name: --presence-penalty
options.description:
Subtract once from logits of tokens already
generated (0 = disabled).

options.name: --frequency-penalty
options.description:
Subtract once per prior occurrence from a
token's logit (0 = disabled).

options.name: --tensor-split
options.description:
(llama.cpp compat) Not supported — OpenTail
places layers with --auto or an explicit -g
<N>.

options.name: --split-mode
options.description:
(llama.cpp compat) Not supported — use --auto
or -g <N> for layer placement.

options.name: --main-gpu
options.description:
(llama.cpp compat) Not supported — use
--device to select the target GPU.

options.name: --mlock
options.description:
(llama.cpp compat) Not implemented in
OpenTail.Stingray. (default: False)

options.name: --no-mmap
options.description: (llama.cpp compat) Not implemented in

options.name: --numa
options.description:
(llama.cpp compat) Not implemented in
OpenTail.Stingray.

options.name: --batch-size
options.description:
(llama.cpp compat) Not supported — OpenTail
does not expose a configurable batch size.

options.name: --ubatch-size
options.description:
(llama.cpp compat) Not supported — OpenTail
does not expose a configurable micro-batch
size.

options.name: --flash-attn
options.description:
(llama.cpp compat) No effect — attention is
already fused in the OpenTail backends.
Accepted with a warning. (default: False)

options.name: --no-warmup
options.description:
(llama.cpp compat) No effect — OpenTail has
no separate warmup step. Accepted with a
warning. (default: False)

options.name: --ignore-preflight
options.description:
Load even if the memory check says the model
will not fit this machine (CPU runs only).

options.name: --backend
options.description:
GPU backend: auto, vulkan, cuda. Default:
auto (prefers CUDA when -g is set and CUDA is
available, otherwise Vulkan).

options.name: --no-thinking
options.description:
Disable reasoning mode (sets
enable_thinking=false in the chat template)

options.name: --allow-unverified-arch
options.description:
Attempt a GGUF whose architecture has no
validated forward-pass profile. Output
correctness is UNVERIFIED: GGUF tensor naming
does not establish compatible attention,
RoPE, normalization or FFN semantics, so the
model may produce plausible but wrong tokens.
Without this flag such a model is refused.

options.name: --thinking
options.description:
Enable reasoning mode (sets
enable_thinking=true). Needed for Gemma 4
reasoning finetunes, which default off
because stock Gemma 4 instruct models aren't
reasoning-trained.

options.name: --hide-thinking
options.description:
Hide reasoning output (the model still
reasons; only the answer is shown) (default:

options.name: --max-thinking-tokens
options.description:
Maximum reasoning tokens before forcing
</think>. 0 = unlimited (default). Not
honored on the speculative-decode path.

options.name: --tools
options.description:
Path to a JSON file of OpenAI-format tool
definitions ([{type:"function",
function:{name, description, parameters}},
...], or a {"tools":[...]} wrapper).
Advertised to the model via its chat
template; on a single-prompt (-p) run the
parsed tool calls are printed after
generation.

options.name: --tool-grammar
options.description:
Constrain tool-call arguments to the --tools
JSON Schemas (issue #374): required keys
can't be dropped, only declared keys/enum
values appear, value shapes match the
declared type. Needs --tools and a model
family with constraint support (Gemma 4,
Qwen/Qwen3-Coder, Llama-3, DeepSeek). Default
off → byte-identical to unconstrained
decoding.

options.name: --json-schema
options.description:
JSON schema to constrain the entire response
to (https://json-schema.org/), e.g.
'{"type":"object","properties":{...},"required":[...]}'
(llama.cpp -j/--json-schema). Root must be an
object schema declaring at least one
property; unsupported keywords ($ref,
oneOf/anyOf, pattern, minLength/maxLength,
minimum/maximum) degrade to unconstrained.
Mutually exclusive with --json-schema-file.

options.name: --json-schema-file
options.description:
File containing a JSON schema to constrain
the entire response to (llama.cpp
--json-schema-file/-jf; alias --jf since
llama.cpp's single-dash -jf isn't
representable: Spectre short options must be
one character). Mutually exclusive with

options.name: --json-schema-ordered
options.description:
With --json-schema/--json-schema-file:
require properties in declaration order
(issue #425) -- optional properties may be
skipped but never reordered. Lets a streaming
consumer act on an early field before a
later, larger one finishes. (default: False)

options.name: --no-moe-predict-prefetch
options.description:
MoE: disable next-layer predictive expert
prefetch (Vulkan; on by default). Env:
STINGRAY_MOE_PREDICT_PREFETCH=0.

options.name: --moe-warmpin
options.description:
MoE: also pin the top-N hottest experts per
layer into the GPU cache after warmup
(default 0 = off; frequency-aware eviction
already retains hot experts). Env:
STINGRAY_MOE_WARMPIN.

options.name: --auto
options.description:
Automatically resolve execution plan based on
hardware and target goal (default: False)

options.name: --goal
options.description:
Optimization goal for execution planning:
balanced (default), quality, throughput,
long-context, low-memory

options.name: --explain
options.description:
Print full decision trace for the resolved
execution plan before starting generation

options.name: --moe-warmpin-after
options.description:
MoE: expert accesses to observe before
warm-pinning selects the hot set (default
512). Only used with --moe-warmpin. Env:
STINGRAY_MOE_WARMPIN_AFTER.

options.name: --expert-stats
options.description:
MoE: write GPU expert-cache (SLRU) hit-rate
stats to this file on exit. Env:
STINGRAY_EXPERT_STATS.

options.name: --cpu-moe
options.description:
MoE: keep ALL routed expert weights on the
CPU (llama.cpp --cpu-moe). Sets
STINGRAY_CPU_MOE=1, overriding the VRAM-fit
auto-select; STINGRAY_CPU_MOE=0 in the env
still forces on-GPU experts. Alias --cmoe
(llama.cpp's single-dash -cmoe isn't
one character). (default: False)

options.name: --n-cpu-moe
options.description:
MoE: keep the routed experts of N layers on
the CPU (llama.cpp --n-cpu-moe). DEFERRED /
not yet supported — OpenTail.Stingray's
expert placement is all-or-nothing (no
per-layer split in the engine), so passing
any value errors with that rationale. Use
--cpu-moe (all on CPU) or omit (auto).

options.name: --gpu-moe-prefill
options.description:
CPU-MoE: run the routed-expert prefill
matmuls on the GPU (transient weight upload,
like llama.cpp's op-offload) instead of CPU
dots. Default ON (#390); pass 'false' to
force the CPU MoE prefill. Sets
STINGRAY_MOE_GPU_PREFILL. ~+28-67% PREFILL on
the CUDA GDN-hybrid CPU-MoE models, with
DECODE within noise of the CPU path — the
register-in-place pin mode
(STINGRAY_MOE_PIN_MODE, default 'register')
cudaHostRegisters the expert mmap pages
instead of a ~14 GB copy, so no RAM duplicate
and no page-cache eviction; a token gate
(STINGRAY_MOE_GPU_PREFILL_MIN_TOKENS, default
64) keeps tiny prefills + decode on the CPU
path. Argmax-stable (GPU runs the MoE in
F32), not bit-identical to CPU.
Auto-falls-back to the CPU path if the GPU
scratch can't allocate.
